strings.d1.s0.name: Playa Delfines
strings.d1.s0.tips: Cancún's biggest free beach: no hotels, turquoise Caribbean water. Check for sargassum season (May-August).
strings.d1.s1.name: Cancún Sign Playa Delfines
strings.d1.s1.tips: Colourful CANCUN letters, a good photo stop.
strings.d1.s2.name: El Fish Fritanga
strings.d1.s2.tips: Local fish restaurant on the lagoon shore. Try the ceviche and tikin xic (Yucatán grilled fish); rare cheap eats for the Hotel Zone.
strings.d1.s3.name: Museo Maya de Cancún
strings.d1.s3.tips: Maya museum with the San Miguelito ruins; an air-conditioned afternoon option.
strings.d1.s4.name: Playa Chac Mool
strings.d1.s4.tips: Central public beach for sunset and waves.
strings.d1.b0.name: Mercado 28 Los De Pescado
strings.d1.b0.tips: Fish tacos in the downtown market, a spot for locals.
strings.d1.b1.name: Playa Tortugas
strings.d1.b1.tips: Calm beach on the lagoon side, next to the ferry pier.
strings.d2.s0.name: Ultramar Ferry Puerto Juárez
strings.d2.s0.tips: 20-minute ferry (about 28 USD return). Rent a golf cart on the island (about 800 MXN).
strings.d2.s1.name: Playa Norte
strings.d2.s1.tips: One of the world's best beaches: shallow and calm, sun loungers 100-200 MXN.
strings.d2.s2.name: Punta Sur Isla Mujeres
strings.d2.s2.tips: The island's southern tip, with the Ixchel temple ruins and a sculpture park. The first sunrise in Mexico.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mango Cafe Isla Mujeres
strings.d2.s3.tips: Caribbean breakfast and lunch; the coconut French toast is the island's famous dish.
strings.d2.s4.name: MUSA Underwater Museum Snorkelling
strings.d2.s4.tips: 500 underwater sculptures. Snorkel tours leave from the pier; take the 17:30 ferry back.
strings.d2.b0.name: Isla Mujeres Mercado Municipal
strings.d2.b0.tips: Cheap local food at the municipal market.
strings.d2.b1.name: Garrafón Reef Park
strings.d2.b1.tips: Zipline and snorkelling park, an alternative to MUSA.
strings.d3.s0.name: Chichén Itzá
strings.d3.s0.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún (ADO bus or tour). See the Kukulkan pyramid and ball court; it's cool and empty at the 08:00 opening. Entry about 697 MXN.
strings.d3.s1.name: Cenote Ik Kil
strings.d3.s1.tips: 5 minutes from Chichén. An open cenote 26 m deep with hanging vines; life jackets are compulsory.
strings.d3.s2.name: Casa Tía Micha Valladolid
strings.d3.s2.tips: Yucatán cuisine in Valladolid: try the cochinita pibil (slow-roast pork) and sopa de lima (lime soup).
strings.d3.s3.name: Calzada de los Frailes Valladolid
strings.d3.s3.tips: A pastel-coloured colonial street leading to the Convent of San Bernardino.
strings.d3.s4.name: Cenote Suytun
strings.d3.s4.tips: Cave cenote with a beam of light. Visit in the afternoon for the light; the drive back takes 2 hours.
strings.d3.b0.name: Cenote Zací Valladolid
strings.d3.b0.tips: A cenote in the town, instead of Suytun.
strings.d3.b1.name: El Mesón del Marqués Valladolid
strings.d3.b1.tips: Colonial restaurant on the main square.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tulum Ruins
strings.d4.s0.tips: 2 hours from Cancún. A Maya fortress by the sea, opening at 08:00. Entry about 95 MXN plus parking, and look out for iguanas.
strings.d4.s1.name: Playa Ruinas Tulum
strings.d4.s1.tips: The beach below the ruins, good for a short swim.
strings.d4.s2.name: Gran Cenote
strings.d4.s2.tips: Cave cenote for snorkelling, with turtles and stalactites. The water is clearest in the morning.
strings.d4.s3.name: Taquería Honorio Tulum
strings.d4.s3.tips: Tulum's legendary breakfast and lunch taco spot. Try the cochinita and lechón (suckling pig); it closes when the food runs out at 14:00.
strings.d4.s4.name: Tulum Beach Road
strings.d4.s4.tips: Palm-lined coastal road. Choose a beach club (Papaya Playa) or a public beach (Playa Paraíso).
strings.d4.b0.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
strings.d4.b0.tips: A cave system with two "eyes", instead of Gran Cenote.
strings.d4.b1.name: Antojitos La Chiapaneca
strings.d4.b1.tips: Al pastor in Tulum town, for the evening.
strings.d5.s0.name: Xel-Há Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: A huge natural aquarium cove with unlimited snorkelling and buffet (about 110 USD). You can swim even in the rain.
strings.d5.s1.name: Xel-Há Buffet
strings.d5.s2.name: Quinta Avenida Playa del Carmen
strings.d5.s2.tips: Playa del Carmen's pedestrian street, for an evening walk and mezcal.
strings.d5.b0.name: Cenote Azul
strings.d5.b0.tips: Open cenote by the roadside, a cheap alternative to Xel-Há.
strings.d5.b1.name: El Fogón Playa del Carmen
strings.d5.b1.tips: Al pastor tacos in Playa, instead of the park.
strings.d6.s0.name: Cozumel Ferry Playa del Carmen
strings.d6.s0.tips: 45-minute ferry from Playa (about 500 MXN return). The Caribbean's best diving island.
strings.d6.s1.name: Palancar Reef Snorkelling
strings.d6.s1.tips: Cozumel's famous reef. Take a boat tour to see turtles and coral.
strings.d6.s2.name: Casa Mission Cozumel
strings.d6.s3.name: Punta Sur Eco Park Cozumel
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lighthouse and crocodile lagoon; you'll need a rental vehicle.
strings.d6.b0.name: Cozumel Sabores
strings.d6.b1.name: Isla Contoy Tour
strings.d6.b1.tips: Bird island with snorkelling off Isla Mujeres, instead of Holbox or Cozumel.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mercado 28
strings.d7.s0.tips: Downtown handicraft market for hammocks and silver. Haggle 40% off.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cocina La Chaya Mercado 28
strings.d7.s1.tips: Yucatán home cooking: panuchos (filled fried tortillas) and chaya juice, a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s2.name: Parque de las Palapas
strings.d7.s2.tips: Downtown square. Marquesitas (crispy crepes) stalls open in the evening; it's quiet by day.
strings.d7.s3.name: ADO Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: ADO bus from the centre to the airport takes 30 minutes.
strings.d7.b0.name: Taquería Los Charros Cancún
strings.d7.b0.tips: Tacos downtown, instead of the market.
strings.d7.b1.name: Playa Langosta
strings.d7.b1.tips: One last swim in the Hotel Zone.
strings.note0: The Hotel Zone R1/R2 bus costs 15 MXN; ADO buses go to Chichén, Tulum and Playa. A rental car gives you freedom for the cenotes (insurance is expensive).
strings.note1: June-November is hurricane season (peak August-October). Expect 33°C, high humidity and afternoon downpours. Sargassum (seaweed) can hit beaches from May to August; Isla Mujeres' Playa Norte stays clean.
strings.note2: Arrive at Chichén Itzá and Tulum for the 08:00 opening; by noon it's 35°C and the tour buses arrive. Non-biodegradable sunscreen is banned in cenotes.
strings.note3: Hotel Zone restaurants cost 3-5 times more; Mercado 28 and the centre (Parque de las Palapas) have local prices. Pay in pesos; the dollar rate is poor.
strings.note4: Tip 10-15%; say "no gracias" to beach vendors. Drink bottled water.
strings.note5: Ferries: Isla Mujeres from Puerto Juárez (Hotel Zone piers are pricey), Cozumel from Playa, Holbox from Chiquilá.
